SECTION I - DESCRIPTION OF PROPOSED ACTION
1.01 Project Purpose. The purpose of the proposed action is to construct a hydroelectric generating plant at the existing Amistad Dam and Reservoir which will provide environmentally clean, fast response energy to replace an equivalent amount generated by fossil fuels. The proposed action includes the integrated operation of the existing International Falcon project and the proposed Amistad hydroelectric plants in a two unit system. The energy thus produced will become a part of the overall total electrical power system covering a very large part of southern Texas.
1.02 Location. The proposed action will be located on the Rio Grande in Val Verde County, Texas, as shown on plate I-1. The powerhouse and appurtenances will be attached to the non-overflow portion of Amistad Dam near the left abutment. This site is approximately 12 miles upstream from Del Rio, Texas.
1.03 Land Requirements. Principal features of the hydroelectric facility, as shown on plate 1-2, would occupy a very small acreage, previously excavated, within the existing project boundary. Of this acreage, all is located on United States Government land, which is administered by the US Section, International Boundary and Water Commission (IBWC). The powerhouse and tailrace channel will occupy space that is now submerged.
Nature of Proposed Action
1.04 Power Plant. The proposed action entails construction, operation, and maintenance of a hydroelectric facility at Amistad Dam and Reservoir by the US Section, IBWC. The power generation facility will consist of a conventional hydroelectric powerhouse and a separate switchyard that would be tied to an existing transmission line. The powerhouse will be a reinforced concrete structure consisting of two generating unit bays, an erection bay, and two service bays. All of the main generating equipment, auxiliary equipment, switch gear and controls, machine tools, utility service equipment and systems, sumps and pumps, oil and compressed air equipment and storage tanks, CO<sub>2</sub> fire protection equipment, offices and visitors facilities will be housed within the powerhouse.
1.05 Generators and Turbines. The powerhouse will contain two synchronous generators direct-connected to vertical shaft, adjustable blade propeller turbines. Each turbine will have a guaranteed output of 22,000 horsepower at 102 feet net head (104 feet gross head), and will have a maximum output of 41,500 horsepower when operating at 208 feet net head (210 feet gross head). Discharges through each turbine will average about 2,000 cfs, but will range between about 2,250 cfs when operating at 102 feet net head, and about 1,900 cfs when operating at 208 feet net head. Each generator will be rated at 28,500 kW nameplate capacity (16,000 kW at minimum head), 30,000 kVA at 0.95 power factor, three-phase, 60 cycles, 13.8 kV, 240 rpm.
1.06 Switchyard. The switchyard will be located above the powerhouse and downstream of the axis of the dam on the United States embankment near the left abutment. The switchyard would contain the 138 kV power transformer, circuit breakers, disconnect and bypass switches, buses, line traps, line coupling capacitors and other related equipment for project control.
1.07 Energy will be delivered through the necessary switches and transformers to the regional high-voltage transmission system supplying the local areas, interconnected plants, and service area of the cooperatives through the Central Power and Light (CP&L) power network.
